name: MCP Guard
summary: MCP proxy that enforces YAML policies on agent tool calls and signs decisions.
use_cases: audit what would be blocked in observe mode

smoke_tests.command: python3 ~/.pickfit/mcp_probe.py --timeout 60 --call hello --args '{}' -- mcp-guard --config pp.config.yaml -- node dummy-server.js

pitfalls.actually_needed: Used `npm install -g @permission-protocol/mcp-guard` so `mcp-guard` is on PATH (~/.local/bin) for offline stdio probe; README shows local `npm install` which does not put it on PATH

Ran `mcp-guard keys init` once plus created `pp.config.yaml` (default_action: allow) and a minimal downstream `dummy-server.js` answering initialize/tools/list/tools/call; without a signing key the guard refuses to start and without a downstream server there is nothing to proxy
`mcp-guard --help` works but `mcp-guard --version` errors with `No server command`

judge.observed: All three screenshots show mcp-guard proxying the dummy server with successful handshake, tool call returning hello world, and help text.

evidence.quote: MCP middleware that blocks dangerous AI agent actions using a simple YAML config
Your agent can no longer delete user data.
Use `observe` mode to audit what *would* be blocked before turning enforcement on.
| API gateway | MCP operates at the tool-call layer, not HTTP. MCP Guard understands tool names and MCP's JSON-RPC protocol. |
| RBAC / IAM | Those gate *users*. MCP Guard gates *agent actions* — the agent is already authenticated, the question is what it's allowed to *do*. |
